text: The undercroft's outer defenses give way after the first assault - Domain-era work, harder than anything Fafnir has built since, and still no match for a full boarding complement as they scramble to reorganize. Your marine commander doesn't have the final count yet.
notes: AddRaidObjective's own success trigger (see XLII_burn_raid_setup above) - fires via FireAll as soon as MarketCMD confirms the objective achieved, mid-result-flow. No options column, so MarketCMD's own remaining result display (marine losses, etc.) continues immediately afterward. Outcome-tier-specific text (clean/caught/revealed) is not here - that's XLII_KoriStrike.showRaidAftermath(), driven by XLII_ResolveBurnRaid's derivation, since the tier isn't known yet at this point in MarketCMD's own flow. Text given a small rewrite (author request, same pass as XLII_burn_raid_setup): added a closing beat ("your marine commander doesn't have the final count yet - give it a minute") to bridge directly into MarketCMD's own immediately-following casualty report, instead of ending on the archive beat alone - the raid is tuned to cost real marines even on a clean run (see XLII_burn_raid_setup's notes on $raidDifficulty), so the text should point at that cost rather than let the objective's completion read as the end of it. Bug fix (author report, this session): this row's own script and XLII_burn_raid_continue's text had been swapped at some point - this row was calling XLII_ResolveBurnRaid (with an empty text) while XLII_burn_raid_continue carried this text with an empty script. Since XLII_ResolveBurnRaid reads $raidMarinesLost, which per this row's own notes above isn't known yet at this mid-flow point, that call was firing too early and swapping the dialog plugin away from MarketCMD's still-in-progress raid-result flow - which is exactly why the chamber/Longsight exploration scene, the August/Ancker interception, and the fleet fight were never actually reached after a completed raid. Swapped both fields back to match what these two rows' own notes always said should happen.

MarketCMD's $raidContinueTrigger (see XLII_burn_raid_setup above) - fires once the entire vanilla raid result flow is done. XLII_ResolveBurnRaid derives the archive-infiltration outcome tier from $raidMarinesLost, applies the caught-tier rep penalty, and reopens XLII_KoriStrike directly in its aftermath state via dialog.setPlugin() - no text/options needed on this row, the Java class takes over rendering immediately. Bug fix (author report, this session): see XLII_burn_raid_success's own notes - this row's script and that row's text had been swapped, so this row was carrying flavor text with an empty script and never actually called XLII_ResolveBurnRaid. Fixed by swapping both fields back.

text:
August's face resolves on a second channel without any request from you. He does not ask how far you got.

"Commander." he says. "It pains me, but I suppose I was wrong about you. An outsider could never understand..."

He does not look away while he says the next part. "I concluded years ago that the alternative to Longsight was Fafnir falling to the first fleet that decided we were worth the trouble. I have never found a version of that where the Alliance survives without it."

"What happens here is not dangerous because you might succeed, Commander. It is dangerous because you might not. Whatever you leave standing, half-broken, does not simply return to what it was before you arrived. It stops needing anyone's permission - mine included."
notes: Fix (author request): this row never actually showed August's portrait - the interaction target throughout this whole XLII_KoriStrike flow is Kori's own entity, not August, and no ShowPersonVisual/ShowSecondPerson command was ever added when this content was written or reframed. Fixed with ShowSecondPerson XLII_fleet_admiral_emil, not a bare/two-arg ShowPersonVisual, because Korrin is already the active first-person portrait at this point (his own from XLII_KoriStrike's chamber scene, showChamberOrb()/showChamberCouncil(), persists across the dialog.setPlugin() swap into this rules.csv chain) - August is joining as a genuine second party, not replacing Korrin. Text's opening line updated to name and place both of them explicitly, per the character-handoff rule (starsector-writing/references/dialogue-mechanics.md) - a portrait command alone doesn't establish the appearance for a reader who's reading text, not watching the portrait swap. Given a real writing pass this session: the confrontation reasoning here already matched August's character bible closely and needed no rewrite; XLII_interception_press and XLII_interception_declare each had one voice-rule violation fixed instead (a "says finally" adverb on a dialogue tag, and a bare "So." fragment - both banned by his own bible's "speaks in complete sentences, always. No fragments"). Fired via dialog.setPlugin(new RuleBasedInteractionDialogPluginImpl(entity, "XLII_interception_open")) from XLII_KoriStrike.showRaidAftermath(), replacing the old direct call to beginAugustScene() - beginAugustScene() is now only reached via the Commit path below, after the fleet fight and boarding sequence. Reuses XLII_burn_state_concern's reasoning almost verbatim (his actual arithmetic about Longsight and Fafnir's survival doesn't need to change) but the surrounding frame flips from "are you certain you want to do this" to "you already did it, and I already know" - see work/outline/main-story-endings.md's section 3, "The interception." No optional digressions like the original chain had ("leave it there for now") - the player is mid-confrontation now, not a voluntary conversation they can politely exit. Endgame redesign, closing line repointed (see .claude/systems/uplink-to-god-endgame-redesign.md): the old line ("What you do here could kill millions... wreck what we've spent tens of cycles building") warned against destroying Longsight, which stopped matching the mechanics the moment Cave moved entirely to before the raid (XLII_KoriStrike's own pre-raid confrontation) - by this point in the story the player has already committed, and the real risk ahead is the fleet fight against the Forty-Second, not the raid already behind them. Also deliberate dramatic irony, not just a fix: "it stops needing anyone's permission - mine included" foreshadows exactly what happens to August specifically if the player fails that fight (see .claude/systems/uplink-to-god-endgame-redesign.md's failure sequence, showFailureDeath()) - he's more right than he knows.

text:
"I understand you came to settle this. I've had the reports since your marines breached the undercroft - I don't need the rest of the explanation from you."

"I know what the AIO told me." He's already looking past you, the way he does once he's made his assessment. "I have always known that is not the same as what the AIO knows. I decided, a long time ago, that the difference was a cost I could afford not to examine."

The one admission of uncertainty he allows himself in a conversation, and he spends it now, on the other side of a fight that's already happened. "I am no longer certain that decision was mine to keep making."
notes: Reuses XLII_burn_press's reasoning, reframed the same way as the row above - his "tell me what changed" no longer makes sense as a request for the player to explain themselves verbally, since the raid already spoke for them.

text:
"No," he says, and the uncertainty is gone from his voice as fast as it appeared. "It is still my decision. What you have done doesn't change whose it is - it only changes what's left of it to make."

"If you finish this, you do it against the Alliance's own doctrine, not with it. The Forty-Second is here because I ordered it here, not because I wanted this fight. What happens next is yours to answer for, not mine."

He straightens - a man taking back control of a room he let slip for exactly one sentence. "Finish it, Commander. There is nothing left here to decide."
notes: Endgame redesign (see .claude/systems/uplink-to-god-endgame-redesign.md) - author-confirmed final piece: Cave is no longer reachable post-raid at all. The closing line and options column both changed from a real fork ("Finish it, Commander, or don't" / Finish it vs. Stand down) to a declaration with a single pacing Continue - August already knows there's nothing left to offer, because the thing that would have stopped him (standing down before the raid) either happened already or didn't; that choice now lives entirely in XLII_KoriStrike's pre-raid confrontation (showAugustInterceptOffer()). Only the closing line and options column changed - the two paragraphs above are untouched, they read fine either way. XLII_interception_cave/_cave_close (below) are deleted as a result - nothing points to them anymore.

text: There is nothing further to discuss. Whatever happens next, happens now.
notes: Commit path. No longer sets $global.XLII_burnTheMachineCommitted - that flag's only reader was XLII_kori_opt_battlegroup_retry, deleted this session along with the standing retry menu it gated (see .claude/systems/uplink-to-god-endgame-redesign.md - losing the fleet fight is now a permanent, consequential failure state, not a free retry loop). Reuses the existing, unmodified XLII_BurnEliasFork rows (XLII_burn_elias_stays/_leaves) verbatim for their own text - only their options column changed (see those two rows' notes) since "return_to_main_menu" doesn't make sense once there's no admiral menu to return to. The FireBest cascade's own text/options display immediately after this row's.

text:
August's link doesn't fully close before Korrin's face replaces it on the display - he was already on the line, uninvited, the way he generally is when it actually matters.

Korrin does not ask if you are sure. He is already pulling up Kori's old maintenance schematics - the ones from his first posting, the ones he was never supposed to still have access to.

"I heard," he says, before you can tell him. "I'm coming. Don't argue with me about it, we don't have the time and you're not going to win."

Something flickers behind the flatness before he puts it away again. "This is the first time in four years I've had an actual answer to that question. Ask me again after, and I still might not be able to tell you what it means that it was this one."
notes: Elias's loyalty fork, high-rep branch. See work/outline/main-story-endings.md, 'Elias Korrin's fork.' Options column changed (this session) from return_to_main_menu to interception_begin_fight - there is no admiral menu to return to anymore; this now starts the fleet fight directly. See XLII_interception_commit's notes.

text:
Word reaches him before you've finished giving the order - he always hears first. When his face appears on the display in August's place, he's already made up his mind.

He does not argue, and he does not come.
